sections.heading: C — Traffic signals
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signals

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals control vehicle and pedestrian movements at intersections. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
On a vertically arranged traffic signal, red occupies the top position and green the bottom. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
On a horizontal traffic signal, red appears at the left and green at the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
A steady red light requires stopping before the marked stop line or crosswalk, or before entering the intersection when neither is marked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
After stopping for a steady red light, wait for green unless an allowed turn on red applies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and traffic, unless a posted sign prohibits that turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A left turn on red is allowed after stopping and yielding from the left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street unless a sign prohibits the turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow light warns that a steady red signal is approaching. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
On approaching a yellow light, reduce speed and prepare to stop, but continue carefully if already in the intersection or unable to stop safely before entering. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
A steady green light permits proceeding through the intersection when the way is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
With a steady green light, turns are allowed unless a sign prohibits them, and turning drivers must yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow requires stopping and normally forbids movement in its direction, but it permits the same lawful turns on red as a steady red light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A01
After stopping for a red arrow, an otherwise permitted turn must yield to pedestrians and traffic, with a right turn barred by a prohibition sign and a left turn limited to the left lane between one-way streets without a prohibiting sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow arrow warns that the movement allowed by the green or flashing yellow arrow is ending and will soon face red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A01
When facing a steady yellow arrow, prepare to stop before entering, but a turn begun under the preceding arrow may be completed cautiously if already inside or unable to stop safely before entry. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A01
A green arrow permits a turn in its indicated direction while opposing traffic is stopped by red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A01
If a green arrow changes to an ordinary green light, the turn remains allowed only after yielding to pedestrians and opposing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light calls for slowing down, watching carefully and proceeding cautiously. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
A flashing red light requires a complete stop, a check in both directions and entry only after the intersection is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow arrow permits a cautious turn only after yielding to pedestrians and opposing traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
The turn under a flashing yellow arrow is unprotected because opposing traffic has a green light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
Treat an inoperative traffic signal as an all-way stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
Ramp-metering lights regulate entry to heavily congested highways and commonly operate during peak rush hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A02
At a metered highway ramp, wait until the signal turns green before entering the highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A02
A single-lane metered ramp admits only one car for each green signal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A02
A ramp with multiple lanes has a separate meter for each lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A02
A green ramp-meter signal does not protect the merge, so the driver must still find a safe traffic gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

Misconceptions: permission from a signal can still require yielding; a green ramp light does not protect the merge; a flashing pedestrian stop signal differs from a steady one.
Mnemonics: identify the signal, locate the allowed movement, then check the required yield.
Glossary: protected turn means opposing traffic is stopped; ramp metering controls entry flow; lane control applies to the lane under the displayed symbol.
Dynamic facts: no officeholder, local answer or time-varying value is asserted; handbook edition currency is tracked as source debt in the authority part.
